subject: Scripts for running CODEX in pararellel on cluster

messages.author: ff7d32384083b3d7
messages.subject: Scripts for running CODEX in pararellel on cluster
parts:
Hello Yuchao,

I have a question about running CODEX in parallel, I need to run over 1000 samples, besides running by chromosomes, any suggestions? Like run CODEX in batches of 200 or 300 samples at a time? I'm wondering how the results affected by the number of samples running at a time, is it the more the better, or it won't affect that much after a certain number (like over 200 or 300 samples)? Thanks!

Best,

Peng

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] Scripts for running CODEX in pararellel on cluster
parts:
Hi Peng,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX. Yes, definitely separate each chromosome and run them in parallel. Also if you have batch information of the 1000 samples, run each batch separately. The latent factors in CODEX can presumably capture these batch effects but if you have these information in advance you don’t need to depend on CODEX. If the batch information is not available, we’ve used the header within the bam file to infer which batch the sample is from.

A side note is that do not set K (the number of latent factors) too high. It is recommended to set it <=10 since the Poisson glm within CODEX sometimes has convergence issue if there are just too many latent factors to estimate.

Hope that this is of help!
Yuchao

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] Scripts for running CODEX in pararellel on cluster
parts:
The largest number that we’ve run so far is around 500 and the smallest is >= 30 samples. We don’t think splitting the sample pool will affect the calling results, if not making it better. Please feel free to let me know if you have further questions. Also we are in the process of releasing CODEX2. Once it is available, we will substitute CODEX and make a public notice on our GitHub page. For relatively rare germline CNV detection (e.g., pop. freq < 20%), CODEX2 and CODEX don’t have too much difference.

Cheers,
Yuchao
